newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem falls 27 pct on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem falls 27 pct on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Sentrachem Ltd fell further on Thursday, shedding 27 percent to 900 cents following an earlier profit warning.

Shares plumbed their lowest level this year falling to 900 cents after the company said forward exchange losses in its Sanachem subsidiary would impact substantially on group profitability in the 1997 financial year.
A dealer on the Johannnesburg Stock Exchange said: "For a company to actually come out and say its profits are going to be down, you know its going to be bad."

Sentrachem said it had become clear that the profitability of Sanachem, which accounted for 10 percent of group operating profit last year, would be knocked because of forward contracts representing 18 months of export trade.
"The Sentrachem group, therefore, has decided to announce that the impact of these issues on the group profitability in the 1997 financial year will be substantial," it said.
John Job, managing director of Sentrachem told Reuters that the forward contracts would reduce Sentrachem's earnings in the 1996/97 financial year by 60 cents a share.
"The fact of the matter is that the decision taken on the forward exchange will mean a 60 cents debit against profits in the current year," Job said.
Although the forward exchange loss would be limited to 60 cents a share, other operational problems at Sanachem could cut further into group profits, he said.
"The foreign exchange issue is limited to 60 cents a share... (but) for operational reasons there could be a further way to go," he said.
Dealers said shares would remain weak on Thursday, but were expected to edge off their lows.
"What usually happens is that people overdo it at the start as they get a fright, but we should see a bit of a recovery later," one dealer said.
Sentrachem said once greater certainty on Sanachem's performance had been reached, the anticipated impact on group earnings would be made known.
Sentrachem said its other four group firms, U.S.-based Hampshire Chemical Corp, Karbochem, NCP and Safripol, were continuing to show improved operating performances compared with last year.
